title: Two trading models caught ZEC’s August breakout. Getting in was only half the story
author: Alphanet_dogwalker
selftext:
I work on AlphaNet (alphanet.global), an automated futures trading platform. One of our strategies, Hackworth Prime, combines several models that make their own entry and exit decisions. This is a look at two of them trading ZEC in August 2026.

For most of the first three weeks, ZEC traded around 455–525. Then it ran from roughly 510 to 836 in five days.

https://preview.redd.it/8j19l5yyj6uh1.png?width=2000&format=png&auto=webp&s=ed8bda09d5a5bed1530d2742b9111b91c9898536

Both models caught that move. But looking at how they got there, and what they held through, tells you more than the final returns.

**The dip buyer got there first, after getting stopped twice**

On Aug 11, one sub-strategy bought into the falling market and was stopped out twice. Its third attempt entered at 471.81.

That entry looks great on the finished chart. The two failed attempts before it are easy to overlook. At the time, it was another entry into a falling market, with no certainty that this attempt would work.

It stayed open through the following quiet week, the breakout and the late-month swings, eventually exiting on Sep 1 at 830.52. That’s a 76.0% move between signal prices, before costs and without subtracting the earlier losses.

https://preview.redd.it/tfd2fbv3k6uh1.png?width=2000&format=png&auto=webp&s=78604244d66a28e8f1cf5f64ecce3b135833b2d1

**The breakout model paid more for confirmation**

The other sub-strategy had already taken a roughly 4% winner inside the range, followed by a stopped trade. It then stayed out for several days.

ZEC broke above 499 on Aug 17. The model entered the following evening at 503.67, after price pulled back toward the old range ceiling.

So it entered about a week later and almost 7% higher than the dip buyer. In exchange, it spent less time exposed before the rally started.

Then on Aug 22, ZEC fell from about 862 to 690 in one four-hour candle. The breakout position’s open gain went from roughly 71% to 37%. Both models stayed in.

The breakout model eventually exited on Aug 29 at 803.28, a 59.5% move from entry. The next day it entered again around 837, above its previous exit.

https://preview.redd.it/bzwlbzick6uh1.png?width=2000&format=png&auto=webp&s=6376c382cba620ff0b018817ef02cb8894621bfa

**Would you have let it finish?**

The dip buyer got stopped twice before catching the move. the breakout model gave back almost half its open profit in one candle, later it sold at 803 and bought back at 837

Each of those moments gives you a pretty convincing reason to step in, stop the strategy and take the profit. In this case, those changes could have cut short the trades that made the month. the models stayed with their signals through the parts that looked bad in isolation.

Thats a big part of following a systematic strategy. You choose a model because you trust the process across a run of trades, then have to let it take trades you wouldnt choose yourself. If you override every uncomfortable decision, the result will be very different.

Following the models worked here. that doesn't make every decision right, but it shows why a good model can still be difficult to follow. The patience was needed before the chart made it look justified

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: The dip buyer getting stopped twice before the winner is the whole story, most people quit after attempt two. Breakout model paying 7% more for confirmation is the tradeoff I'd take every time, less time exposed to chop.

replies.author: Alphanet_dogwalker
replies.body: yeah the later entry skipped about a week of waiting. It still sat through that 20% drop though, so paying more for confirmation didn't make the rest of the trade easy. that's the bit i found interesting with these two, very different entries but the same uncomfortable hold once they were both in

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Thanks for the disclosure, and for showing the two stopped trades and the 20% single-candle drop instead of only the finish. A single winning month on one asset can't show whether holding through those moments pays on average, so I'd look at the full list of trades from both models across several months and assets, including the periods where holding through a drop ended badly. Also report the combined result net of fees and funding, with the sum of all the stopped trades, since the 76% move excludes them. Spot moves like ZEC's often line up with news or listing events, and Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for macro releases) is one source for checking whether the entries lined up with scheduled catalysts.

comments.author: Urselff
comments.body: Which AI are these, ChatGPT or Claude?

replies.author: Alphanet_dogwalker
replies.body: Neither, these are AlphaNet's own deep learning models. The dip buyer and breakout model are separate parts of Hackworth Prime, each producing its own signals. No LLMs here, should've made that clearer up front
